news.title: Argentina taunt England with commemorative day to celebrate World Cup win
news.lede: Argentina’s post-match celebrations against England were shrouded in controversy (Picture: EPA) The Argentine Football Association has created a special day to commemorate their side’s victory over England at the 2026 World Cup. England and Argentina renewed their fierce rivalry for the first time in 21 years when both sides reached the semi-finals of this summer’s World Cup. The fixture came 40 years on from England’s infamous 2-1 defeat to the Albiceleste, made famous by Diego Maradona’s controversial ‘Hand of God’ goal that secured a 2-1 win for Argentina. And while England took the lead this time around through Anthony Gordon’s second-half strike, the Three Lions fell to a heartbreaking defeat by the same scoreline after two late Argentina goals.

news.title: Argentina announce 'National Football Teams Day' to celebrate dramatic 2026 World Cup victory over England
news.lede: The Argentine Football Association has officially declared July 15 as 'National Football Teams Day' to commemorate their historic 2026 World Cup semi-final triumph over England. The date immortalises a dramatic comeback in Atlanta where the Albiceleste scored twice in the final minutes to shatter English dreams and secure their place in a second consecutive final. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has moved to permanently celebrate the date of their most recent major victory over their rivals. Following a unanimous vote by the council executive meeting, July 15 will now be recognised as a day of national sporting significance.

news.title: How to fix Fifa: what can be done to salvage football’s beleaguered governing body?
news.lede: Gianni Infantino followed World Cup controversies with a widely scorned plan to let private investors in. Here’s how the game’s leaders can find a path forward. How can an organisation that runs the biggest sporting event in the world also be the one that sets the rules for the entire game? We saw the reality of such a conflict at the recent World Cup as Fifa ran roughshod over its rulebook – be it over the length of suspensions or the duration of half-time – in an attempt to generate more attention for its competition.

news.title: Canada PM Carney says has no confidence in Fifa’s Infantino
news.lede: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney (right), whose country co-hosted the 2026 World Cup, has joined growing criticism of Fifa president Gianni Infantino. (EPA Images pic) TORONTO: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney, whose country co-hosted the 2026 World Cup, joined Wednesday an international chorus of criticism of Gianni Infantino, saying he no longer had confidence in his ability to lead Fifa. "Certainly I don't have confidence in Mr Infantino, after this point, given what transpired," Carney told reporters when asked about Fifa's chief and his now-shelved plan to open the World Cup up to private investment. Infantino has come under increasing pressure, even from within his organisation, over his handling of the proposal, and calls for him to step down have grown since he abandoned it last Saturday.
